A: At 1600x1000 the triage queue is entirely below the fold; KPI strip + large 24h chart + 40-client grid fill the first viewport, contradicting the DECISIONS claim of a triage-first hierarchy - the most urgent alert is not visible in 3 seconds, only the 'Critical open 6' count
Internal data inconsistency: KPI says 'Open alerts 1,284' while the queue says '64 of 64 queued alerts' and client-estate open counts sum to ~64, with no reconciling label
Queue panel shows ~10 rows in a fixed scroll region with large unused vertical space below it on the full page - poor density for a 64-alert triage list
In the trend chart, saturated blue (Low) and yellow (Medium) visually dominate the critical red segments, inverting attention priority
Severity is colour + text label only, no shape glyph; detail panel shows 'Cobalt Freight / Industry: Health' (placeholder mismatch, cosmetic)
B: Alert-detail column has substantial dead space below the content on tall viewports
Below ~860px the client rail and detail panel are cut off (self-declared desktop-only trade-off; no responsive fallback for narrow windows)
24h trend is a compact tile rather than a full panel - adequate but the least developed of the four required views; hour-axis labels limited to -24h/-12h/now
Volume legend counts (3/20/126 = 149) sit directly under open counts (131) without an explicit 'intake vs open' label, mildly confusable

notes: Both are single-file, dependency-free, working dashboards with real filters, row-driven detail panels, keyboard support and labelled (not colour-only) severity. B wins on the core triage test: the queue with SLA countdowns is the primary region and the breached critical is readable in seconds, severity is triple-coded (shape+label+colour), stale telemetry is surfaced as 'stale != clear', and its numbers are internally consistent. A is polished and well-verified but buries the queue below the fold behind a chart and a 40-client grid, and its headline 1,284 'open alerts' contradicts its own 64-alert queue.
